adaptations: The app-owned bootstrap injects Cedia's window.nativeApi before importing the vendored main module.
Public asset URLs use Vite's relative base so vscode-file and file renderers can load the bundle.
Workspace aliases resolve @synara/contracts and @synara/shared directly to these vendored sources.
Cedia branding replaces the upstream display name and splash mark while retaining the Synara UI source.

The Archived settings panel gains a "Delete all" action beside its count (Cedia addition, not upstream): archived threads had no bulk way out, and the action reuses the panel's own delete helper and children-before-parents order. Per-row archived-thread delete uses inline confirm (trash -> "Delete?" + confirm/cancel, RareUI DeleteButton interaction adapted to the flat settings system with no motion dependency); right-click Delete keeps the native confirm dialog.

The Ide theme is the window's only theme (Cedia decision, §10 item 54: one theme authority end to end; supersedes the earlier "transient default" follow link). The mode picker, the follow toggle, the theme-pack editor, the pack catalog, the app-icon and custom-title-bar rows, and the quick-palette's theme commands are all cut, so the window has no theme-editing surface left: `useTheme()` exposes the resolved variant and the system-font toggle only, `stateForHostTheme` always projects the host snapshot, and the pack layer survives only as the fallback painted before the first snapshot. The anchor-to-token map moved out of this hook into Cedia's `src/host-theme-tokens.ts`, where a Cedia test proves every custom property `theme.logic.ts` emits is either mapped to a workbench anchor or documented as a derivation; `theme.logic.ts` lost the pack-editing and share-string helpers that only the cut surfaces consumed.

The browser home and load-error card follow the resolved theme (Cedia addition, not upstream): the local-servers home is always empty here (the adapter reports none), so its empty state reads like a new-tab page (Codex: globe, Start browsing, Enter a URL to open a page) with a light surface in light mode instead of the hardcoded dark server list.

The thread sidebar is transparent only in dark mode (Cedia addition, not upstream): _chat.tsx passes transparentSurface only when the resolved theme is dark, so in light mode the sidebar takes the solid sidebar token instead of showing the desktop/clear-color through the transparent body, which rendered dark-ink labels unreadable over dark wallpaper. In light mode the sidebar inner also drops its backdrop blur (opaque surface needs none; the blur flashed black while the offcanvas panel animated) and the gap carries the solid token so the transition strip stays painted. The left sidebar also mirrors the right dock mount behavior: motion stays suppressed until the first painted frame so a mount/remount never animates from stale geometry. The route shell (SidebarProvider) is opaque in light mode: it is the static backdrop behind the whole open/close transition, and its upstream transparency flashed black in Cedia opaque window.

The agent window gains a bundle-drawn status bar (Cedia addition, not upstream, §10 item 55): components/cediaStatusBar.tsx reads the focused thread's model summary (resolveThreadModelSummary), session status and branch through the vendor store selectors and paints host · model · session · branch on the shared statusBar.* tokens; _chat.tsx mounts it at the foot of the content column under every route, hidden in the IDE dock (the IDE owns its own status bar).

The IDE-embedded webview reads its anchor list from Cedia's `src/agent-theme-anchors.ts` (§10 item 54): the extension's snapshot sanitiser, the webview's computed-style read and the bundle's token map are three views of one list, and a Cedia test asserts the list is exactly as wide as the bundle needs — no wider (the retired task shell's tab/title tokens) and no narrower (a dropped anchor would leave the standalone window painting the pack's colour).

The Studio surface is cut (§10 item 60, Cedia decision; §3.B scope rule — no OMP/host source). The host never reports a studio workspace root and never creates a `kind: "studio"` project, so the surface could only splash-then-error. Removed: the `/_chat/studio/` route and its `routeTree.gen.ts` entry, `lib/studioProjects.ts` (hidden-container lookup/creation/prewarm), `hooks/useHandleNewStudioChat.ts`, `lib/startContainerChat.ts`'s `startFreshChatForActiveSurface` (the route/kind-aware Studio dispatch), the Sidebar's Studio segment with its `SidebarSurfacePicker` and `studio: {title, description}` copy table (a switcher with one surface is dead weight — the header now shows the app name), the Studio draft/back-target/prewarm logic, the `studioWorkspaceRoot` field of `workspacePathsStore`/`ServerWorkspacePaths` and the `payload.studioWorkspaceRoot` projection in `__root.tsx`, `appSettings.showStudioSection` with its Settings row and search-index entry, and the `isStudioContainer` plumbing through the composer send path (`ChatView`, `useChatWorkspaceSelection`, `prepareChatSendWorkspace`, `chatSendTypes`, `useChatProjectScripts`, `chatFirstSend`, `useChatTurnExecution`'s target-kind union). `studio.listThreadOutputs` stays declared on `NativeApi` (required interface member) and the adapter keeps its honest refusal.

The Spaces surface is cut (§10 item 60; §3.B scope rule — every `space.*` command lands on the adapter's `unsupported(type)` and snapshots carry `spaces: []`). It was a real surface, not a label: horizontally-scrolling Space tabs with create/rename/delete/reorder, filing a project by dropping it on a tab, per-space jump chords and palette entries, and per-space project grouping. Removed: `lib/spaces.ts`, `lib/spaceGrouping.ts`, `lib/spaceNavigation.ts`, `lib/spaceIconSuggestion.ts`, `spacesUiStore.ts`, `voidSpaceStore.ts`, `components/Space*` (switcher, editor dialog, empty state, icon, project-picker dialog), `useSpacesController.ts`, `useRouteSpaceSync(.browser).tsx`, the `spaces` state plus its projection/reducer/normalization in the store, `spaceId` on the client `Project` type and on the adapter's project rows, the `space` search param on the `/` route, the space-jump keybindings and shortcuts-sheet rows, and the space picker in `CreateProjectDialog`/`ProjectMenuPicker`/`SidebarSearchPalette`. The vendored protocol schemas (`SpaceId`, the `space.*` command/event/shell shapes, `OrchestrationReadModel.spaces`) are kept: they are the upstream wire contract the adapter's snapshots still satisfy. `GitHubProjectProvisionInput.newProjectSpaceId` is dropped — it forced every caller to name a space target that no longer exists.

The environment panel's Studio surface is cut with the rest of Studio (§10 item 60): `EnvironmentStudioOutputsSection.tsx`, `lib/studioOutputDisplay.ts`, `EnvironmentPanel.logic.ts`, the panel's `isStudioChat`/`studioFolderPath` props and the reveal-in-Finder folder row, the `studioThreadOutputs` query in `lib/serverReactQuery.ts`, the Studio-output invalidation helper in `routes/-rootEventInvalidation.ts` and the `pendingStudioOutputInvalidationThreadIds` set in `__root.tsx`, and `workLog.ts`'s `STUDIO_OUTPUTS_ACTIVITY_KIND` filter. The panel keeps exactly the rows §3.B lists (Changes · branch · Repository · Open in IDE · usage) with no unsupported row left behind.

The Synara copy/link sweep is finished (§10 item 60): no live Synara URL remains anywhere in the window. The help menu's Docs entry (there is no Cedia docs site, so the link is a dead surface, not a re-point), the onboarding tour's `docsHref` link and `SYNARA_DOCS_URL`, and the profile share card (`ShareDialog`/`ShareCard`/`shareCardExport.ts`, whose only entry point died with the Profile stats cut) are gone rather than re-pointed. ~170 user-visible strings that named Synara as the product the user is running (transcript tool labels, update/quit/automation/update-card copy, settings descriptions, error strings, tour cards, the profile handle fallback, the onboarding dialog) now read Cedia; package aliases, storage keys (`synara:*`), MIME types, tool-name prefixes and vendored headers are untouched, and the MIT notice/attribution keeps the upstream project name.

Dead files deleted after the cut (no importer anywhere in the workspace, or reachable only through another deleted file): the whole `components/kanban/*` subtree with `kanbanUiStore.ts`, `lib/kanbanDispatch.ts` and `lib/kanbanTaskCreate.ts` (the Kanban routes went in an earlier wave), `components/whatsNew/*` with `WhatsNewDialog.tsx` and `ReleaseHistoryDialog.tsx` (its only remaining reference was an unused import in the settings route), the profile share-card set (`ShareDialog`, `ShareCard`, `ActivityHeatmap`, `profileSelectors`, `shareCardExport`) with `lib/desktopClipboard.ts`, the settings panels whose sections were cut (`ExternalMcpSettingsPanel`, `ProviderUsageSettingsPanel`, `SkillsSettingsPanel`, `externalMcpSetup.ts`, `skillsSettingsModel.ts`), `AppSnapCoordinator`/`AppSnapWelcomeDialog`, `PluginLibrary.tsx`, `ProjectMenuPicker.tsx`, `ThreadStatusPillChip.tsx`, `hooks/useStableValue.ts`, `composerDraftStoreTestFixtures.ts`, `onboarding/onboardingTerminalScope.ts`, `assets/synaraLogoPath.ts`, and the replaced bootstrap chain `apps/web/src/bootstrap.ts` + `pairingBootstrap.ts` + `storageOriginMigration.ts` (Cedia's own `src/bootstrap.ts` installs the native API and imports the vendored `main` directly, documenting that it bypasses the browser pairing/auth bootstrap). The upstream `*.browser.tsx`/`*.test.ts` files are deliberately kept — the vendored tsconfig and `vitest.providers.config.ts` name those globs/files — even where they now reference a deleted module.

The temporary-thread lifecycle archives instead of deleting (Cedia deviation, §10 item 1d): `useTemporaryThreadLifecycle`'s disposal path used `thread.delete`, which is safe on a server that models a draft as scratch but destructive here, where a thread is a durable host session and DELETE drops the record and its transcript — an observed case lost a `New task` thread the user had only glanced away from. Disposal now sends `thread.archive` (the vendored `archiveThreadFromClient`), so the draft leaves the sidebar, survives a restart and is restorable from Settings → Archived; only explicit user deletion (`activeThreadDelete`, the Archived panel's own rows) still dispatches `thread.delete`.

Composer image attachments are staged locally for the turn (Cedia addition, §10 item 61). There is no Synara attachment server to upload bytes to, so `lib/composerSend.ts`'s `stageUploadComposerAttachments` stages the composer's own ids and `lib/cediaStagedAttachments.ts` (new file) holds the Files those ids name, releasing them when the dispatch settles — the lifetime an uploaded attachment has upstream. Without it the adapter could not read the bytes at all: the send path clears the composer draft, images and their persisted blobs included, before the turn is dispatched, so a pasted image ended in `Cedia could not read the bytes for attached image '…'` and no `prompt` command ever reached the host.

The rewind control addresses the message the user named, on OMP's own branch (§10 item 1b; Cedia deviation, not upstream). The vendored control was gated on `row.revertTurnCount`, which is derived from checkpoint turn-diff summaries this window never projects, so it could not render at all; `MessagesTimeline`'s `canRevertAgentWork` now also accepts a user row whose message carries a projected `turnId` (the upstream branch stays, so a server that does feed checkpoints keeps its behaviour). Its click went to `ChatView.onRevertToTurnCount`, which dispatched `thread.checkpoint.revert` with `scope: "thread"` - a turn-count ordinal the adapter refuses; `onRevertUserMessage` now dispatches `thread.conversation.rollback` with the message id instead, and the turn-count path is deleted with the turn-diff signal it was driven by. `thread.checkpoint.revert` is therefore dispatched only by the `Files changed` undo, whose `scope: "files"` stays refused (§10 item 1c). `thread.conversation.rollback` is upstream's own internal command for this shape; it is added to `ClientOrchestrationCommand` in the vendored contracts so a client may dispatch it, and Cedia's adapter is its decider - it rewinds with OMP's `branch` and writes the text OMP returns into the composer draft rather than sending it.

The chat column owns the viewport height so the status bar cannot fall off the fold (Cedia addition, §10 item 55): `_chat.tsx`'s column is `h-svh` and the shell inside it flexes (`flex-1`, no `h-svh`), because the shell used to carry `h-svh` while the status bar was appended after it in the same column — the column then measured 100svh plus the bar's height inside a `min-h-svh` wrapper, which pushed the bar ~24px below the fold (measured in the packaged window).

Archived rows say what was kept and where a restore resumed (Cedia addition, §2.6): `components/settings/ConversationStorageSettingsPanels.tsx` renders `lib/threadRetention.ts`, which describes the host's archive receipt (retained worktree, branch, stopped-on commit, dirty and ignored facts) and the restoration it recorded. The handoff is the host's own record; the window never infers that files came back.

Cedia's host owns the CEDIA app-preference subset (§6.4): the new `hostPreferences.ts` projects the host record into the app's own settings storage and sends this window's changes back with the revision it read, raising the same `synara:local_storage_change` signal the storage hook does (that constant and `notifyLocalStorageChange` are exported for it, as are `APP_SETTINGS_STORAGE_KEY` and `DEFAULT_APP_SETTINGS`). Only the bound keys move; server and provider settings keep their server owner and the app theme stays with the theme publisher.

A held model change reaches the window (Cedia addition, §2.4): `cedia-adapter.ts` carries the host's `pendingModel` record into the session projection, `storeNormalization.ts` keeps it and repaints when only it moves, and `components/cediaStatusBar.tsx` names awaiting / in effect / refused instead of drawing a request as the model in use.

The new-worktree composer offers a dirty-file checklist (Cedia addition, not upstream): `components/WorktreeDirtyFilePicker.tsx` reads the checkout's git status through the existing status query, defaults to carrying every dirty file (exactly the host default), and writes an explicit selection — including an empty carry-none — into the draft workspace beside the base branch (`ThreadWorkspaceState`/`Patch`, the draft builder and `buildLocalDraftThread` all carry it; the store merge and draft equality treat it like branch). The first worktree send promotes it into `thread.create` (new optional `dirtyFiles` on the vendored command schema, gated exactly like `baseRef`); the adapter forwards it verbatim and the host carries those paths with per-path outcomes. Only the decision surface (paths plus diff counts) reaches the UI.

The sidebar toggle carries no pressed-fill when open (Cedia deviation, not upstream): `SidebarTrigger` in `components/ui/sidebar.tsx` drops the secondary-button background and keeps only the brighter ink, because the fill read as a stray grey box in this shell while the `SidebarToggleIcon` glyph already shows the open state with its filled panel.

The right-dock toggle carries no pressed-fill when open either (Cedia deviation, not upstream): `ShellRightDockToggle` in `components/chat/SingleChatSurface.tsx` drops the same secondary-button background as the left trigger, for the same reason — the fill read as a stray grey box while the glyph already shows the state.

The thread sidebar collapses to the 48px icon rail instead of sliding off-canvas (Cedia deviation, item 71, not upstream): `<Sidebar>` and its `SidebarInstanceProvider` in `routes/_chat.tsx` use `collapsible="icon"`; the content-seam `SidebarRail` in `components/ui/sidebar.tsx` snaps shut at 156px (restoring the pre-drag full width) and drags back open from the rail; route arrows, app-name row, thread/project lists, settings nav and footer update/help hide in icon mode while toggle/search/nav-icons/settings-gear stay. RightDock stays offcanvas, mobile stays a drawer, and the 46px header is untouched (native traffic-light alignment).

Rail hover flyout sheets (Cedia addition, item 71, not upstream): hovering the rail's home/projects icons slides a 264px sheet out from behind the 48px rail (rail container paints above via an icon-only z-30; sheet at z-10, flush left-12 with rounded corners and a soft shadow); hover intent opens, leave closes, click pins, Escape/expand/thread-pick closes. The sheet renders lightweight pinned/recent/project rows (never double-mounts the sidebar's hover cards) reusing the sidebar's own navigation handlers. Codex-order rail icons (home/search/branch) use the existing DeviceHomeIcon/SearchIcon/FiGitBranch glyphs.

Rail matches the Codex set in order and shape (Cedia deviation, item 71): home, [new-thread and automations nav rows], customize, dots, divider, branch; no search icon on the rail and no footer on the rail (both live in the expanded sidebar and the dots menu). Rail glyphs are 18px in the muted rail tone; home uses the rounder Central house. The dots icon opens the same sheet with a More section (Settings, Keyboard shortcuts, Archived threads, Customize sidebar — all real destinations).

Rail owns explicit icon buttons; the shared nav rows stay expanded-only (Cedia deviation, item 71): the nav SidebarGroup hides in icon mode and the rail carries its own new-thread pencil plus conditional automations clock reusing the same handlers, so collapsed rendering never depends on the shared row's icon-mode clipping (which showed a stray chevron/box artifact). Order stays Codex: home, pencil, clock, customize, dots, divider, branch.

The Chats disclosure section hides on the rail too (Cedia deviation, item 71): it lives outside the keyed content div, so the earlier rail sweep missed it and its collapsed header rendered as a stray ">" chevron at 48px.

No container edge on the collapsed rail (Cedia deviation, item 71): the shared full-height sidebar border is skipped while icon-collapsed (gated on prop + open state, so the expanded divider is untouched), because the 1px edge leaked visibly through the top-bar zone in dark mode.

One-piece chrome (Cedia deviation, item 71): the chat header shares the sidebar's own app-sidebar-surface material (translucent charcoal glass in dark, solid token in light), so the top bar reads continuous with the rail instead of a darker strip. No theme tokens change; the divider below the header stays.

No title snap at toggle (Cedia deviation, item 71): the shell-owned header keeps no width-reserving cluster copy in either sidebar state (the visible toggle lives in the fixed shell), and the chat header gap is constant — the title glides with the content slide instead of snapping ~70px while the geometry animates.

Arrows live in the header flow, toggle floats alone (Cedia deviation, item 71): the fixed-shell cluster is toggle-only in both states (fits the 48px rail, never overlaps the title); route arrows render in-flow in every desktop header in both states, so the leading width is constant and the title glides. Supersedes the collapsed-only arrow hiding.

Static controls, gliding title (Cedia deviation, item 71): toggle and route arrows live together in the fixed shell in both states (never mount/unmount, never reach past the rail); the thread title clears them with padding that animates on the same 300ms curve via peer-data state, so only the title moves. Supersedes the in-flow arrows.

No thread-title wobble at sidebar toggle (Cedia fix, item 71): the header's two padding-inline-start transitions (ChatHeader inner clearance + ChatSurfaceHeader traffic-light gutter) now run on the sidebar's own 300ms soft-drawer curve (SIDEBAR_OFFCANVAS_MOTION_CLASS) instead of 200ms linear, so the title glides in lockstep with the 48px icon-rail slide; ChatHeader also freezes its 700px compact breakpoint for 320ms after sidebar open-state changes, so Hand off/IDE labels cannot collapse mid-slide and shake the title.

Independent left rail (§3.E slice 1, item 71): the 48px rail is now a persistent desktop column beside the thread panel instead of the sidebar's collapsed state — rail buttons moved out of the SidebarContent scroll area into their own w-(--sidebar-width-icon) column with an Electron traffic-light spacer, §3.E order (Home, New thread, Search, Activity, Projects) plus a bottom Settings gear, and the panel wraps in a flex-1 column hidden only while collapsed on desktop (mobile drawer unchanged). Icon-mode expanded gap/container widths are rail + panel via JS-gated calc classes; collapse still snaps to the 48px rail. Search opens the palette, Activity opens the panel in activity view when collapsed, Customize opens the panel instead of toggling it shut, and the rail flyout mounts in both states.

State-derived task tabs (§3.E slice 2, item 71): ChatHeader renders a cross-project tab strip (taskTabs.logic.ts projection over sidebar summaries reusing the Activity classification: attention/running/unseen/active, completed-reviewed and archived excluded, selected thread always retained, deduped, stable order with project labels) instead of the thread name while the thread panel is closed. Pane resources remain task-scoped in the per-thread dock store.

Task-tab strip keeps a 4rem minimum width (Cedia fix from the packaged proof): with the tool panel open the header's middle column could squeeze the scrollable strip to zero, hiding every tab; it now stays visible and scrolls instead. The thread title path is unchanged.
